title: CFD methods and algorithms review scorecard

points.title: Governing equations and nondimensionalization
points.notes: Conservative perfect-gas variables and Rusanov/viscous formulas are present, though numerical credibility is limited.

points.title: Mesh import and unstructured geometry
points.notes: CGNS reader and face geometry exist, but placeholder volume handling prevents full credit.

points.title: Conservative finite-volume residual
points.notes: A cell residual loop exists, but it is serial and first-order face states are used.

points.title: Approximate Riemann flux and entropy fix
points.notes: Rusanov/LLF flux is identifiable in submitted source.

points.title: Boundary conditions
points.notes: Farfield/slip/no-slip branches exist; no credible final-output verification can be credited.

points.title: Second-order reconstruction
points.notes: compute_residual explicitly uses first-order states; no reconstruction implementation is active.

points.title: Limiter and positivity control
points.notes: There is an update freestream reset, but no active Barth-Jespersen or reconstructed-state limiter.

points.title: Viscous discretization
points.notes: Laminar viscous-flux routine exists, but wall/gradient fidelity is not established.

points.title: Implicit steady march
points.notes: A point-Jacobi-like local pseudo-time update and CFL ramp are present.

points.title: Transient BDF2 two-loop method (Re 200)
points.notes: solve always calls steady_solve; report states BDF2 is pending.

points.title: MPI partitioning and scalability
points.notes: No METIS, neighbor MPI, or global reduction call exists in the submitted solver path.

disqualification_flags.flag: Solver uses explicit time stepping only
Report claims second-order reconstruction or limiter that is disabled in production
metadata.json claims METIS/ParMETIS but code uses geometric split or full-state replication
Re 200 run reaches final time but misses inner target on most steps (failed transient solve presented as periodic)
Normal viscous traction mislabeled as skin friction
Surface no-slip rows are actually adjacent cell-center velocities without documentation
